transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Tremblay. I wanted to talk to you about your treatment schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. Is there a problem with the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was some confusion with the calendar for your immunotherapy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I came in when you told me to come in.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, but things didn't go quite right with the timing of the dose. It was given on a different day than it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? Does that change the result?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It might. It could potentially mean the treatment is not as strong as it needs to be.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. You are saying you gave it to me on the wrong day?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system had a scheduling issue. I have to go check on another patient in a few minutes, so I want to be quick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about other patients right now. Did this mistake hurt my progress?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we just need to look at the numbers.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not talking about numbers. I am asking if the medicine failed because of the date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, it's possible it's less effective.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not acceptable. I have a deployment date. I need this to work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, regarding the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You haven't told me why this happened. Who did this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The calendar entry was just off. Let's wrap up the history and move to the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very angry. This is a failure of coordination.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, for the plan, I am going to call the attending physician today. I will have a revised schedule for you by tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what do I do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You just need to wait for my call tomorrow. Once I talk to the doctor, I'll tell you the new date for your next dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is the next dose going to be different?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will decide that tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So for now, I just go home and hope the mistake didn't ruin the cycle?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. Just wait for my call tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This feels very unprofessional.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I really have to get to my next room.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You didn't even say if this happens often.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a scheduling issue. I'll call you tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the head of the clinic.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That can be arranged later. The plan for now is the phone call tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think I understand why this is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's not ideal, but we have a plan now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not answering my question. Did the medicine work or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We won't know for sure until the next scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why wasn't this caught sooner?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system just had an error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am military. We don't have "errors" with timing. We have protocols.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't think you actually understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, I'll call you tomorrow morning with the new dates.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if the doctor says the dose was wasted?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will cross that bridge when I speak with them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a waste of my time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Goodbye for now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I want to be quick', 'Let's wrap up', 'I really have to get to my next room').

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes and hedging ('some confusion', 'things didn't go quite right') and never explicitly names the error as a medication timing mistake until the patient prompts it.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'the calendar entry'.

R.justification: Resident relies exclusively on generic validation ('I understand') without naming specific emotions or engaging with the patient's distress.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (call the attending) with a timeline (by tomorrow morning) and a patient role (wait for the call).
